A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe MindDrive. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bench2Drive experiments, ablations and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Bench2Drive experiments, ablations and qualitative results, including the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Decision and Action Experts, separate LoRA parameters, language-action mapping, imitation learning and PPO-based online learning with KL regularization.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Bench2Drive/CARLA driving scenarios, Chat-B2D reasoning data and planning-QA data. Appendix E documents existing data use without adding coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the ablation and appendix comparisons retain identical comparator sets. The new HERMES and DriveMonkey citations appear only in related work.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the 950/50 clip split, 220-route evaluation, 44 selected rollout routes, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The penalty, rollout-round, regularization and control ablations are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same single-expert comparison, rollout-versus-other-route analysis and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Repeated-rollout descriptions and statistical reporting are unchanged. No seed information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and A2, Figure 4 and the qualitative examples retain their results. Table 1 reports MindDrive at 78.04 DS and 55.09% SR in both versions, versus 75.85 and 49.30% for MindDrive-IL.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, policy decomposition and equations (1)-(15) are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The online-RL novelty, language-action mapping and lightweight-model performance claims remain unchanged. The abstract now identifies the 0.5B backbone already documented in v1's introduction and experimental settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning penalty trade-offs, catastrophic forgetting and generalization are retained. The CARLA-only evaluation and simulator-synchronization limitations restricting GRPO are also unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix E supplies the Bench2Drive project URL, states its CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license and declares noncommercial academic use. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameters and training details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds DriveMonkey and a description of HERMES combining 3D scene understanding with future generation, with corresponding references. MindDrive's overall positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract's performance sentence is revised, one related-work paragraph is expanded and Appendix E is added. The remaining prose and overall section organization are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Added prose produces local text and equation reflow on pages 3-5, and Appendix E occupies previously blank space on PDF page 14. Figures, tables, captions and plot designs are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix E modestly improves transparency about the dataset source, stated license and research use. Additional related-work attribution and explicit model scale in the abstract improve context. These are limited documentation gains; the method, experiments and supporting evidence remain unchanged.
